chunks: "Sleeping at the beginning of the day is wastefulness, the midday nap is a blessing, sleeping after al-'Asr is foolishness, and sleeping between the two night prayers deprives one of sustenance."

key_terms.أَوَّلَ النَّهَارِ: the beginning of the day; early daytime after dawn
key_terms.النَّوْمُ: sleep; the act of sleeping discussed in different parts of the day
key_terms.الْعِشَاءَيْنِ: the two evening prayers, meaning Maghrib and 'Isha'
key_terms.حُمْقٌ: foolishness or lack of sound judgment
key_terms.خُرْقٌ: wastefulness or foolish imprudence in conduct

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Baqir عليه السلام say about disliked and recommended times for sleeping?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches proper daily conduct by distinguishing blameworthy and praiseworthy times for sleep. It presents early daytime sleep, post-'Asr sleep, and sleep between Maghrib and 'Isha' negatively, while describing the midday nap as a blessing, linking personal discipline with one's livelihood.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: "Sleeping at the beginning of the day is wastefulness, the nap at midday is a blessing, sleeping after Asr (afternoon prayer) is foolishness, and sleeping between the two night prayers (Maghrib and Isha) deprives one of sustenance."
